## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Select the recovery scenario and critical data

agent-runnable


Identify the service, data dependencies, recovery point and outage scenario to test. Confirm the approved recovery objectives and authorized test environment, including keys, identities and external dependencies.

- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Approve the exercise safeguards and owners

human · human approval required


The accountable service and security owners approve the test scope, isolation, communication and stop conditions. Protect production and sensitive data and confirm who may authorize destructive or customer-affecting actions.

- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Restore the selected backup in isolation

manual form/portal · human approval required · hard to undo


Authorized operators recover the approved backup, dependencies and access using the documented runbook. Record actual times, failures and deviations without overwriting the production system.

- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Verify data integrity and business operation

agent-runnable


Check completeness, consistency and the agreed business transactions in the restored environment. Compare actual data loss and recovery time with objectives and distinguish a readable backup from a usable service.

- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Approve remediation and a repeat test

human · human approval required


Owners review the evidence, assign fixes and retest failed controls. Update the runbook and recovery assumptions and retain the exercise result and unresolved risks.

- Verify: A measured recovery result against approved objectives, with failed dependencies assigned and retested.
- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)
